title: Video foundations
summary: The Video half of MM ACF. Same layer ladder, same spec-card template, same bin model as the Image half — appended below it, sharing one file so reuse is literal rather than described.

sections.title: Video-specific rules
sections.body: The behaviours that separate video from image and that ACF cannot express generically. Everything here is MM-owned policy, not a token.

sections.title: Aspect ratios
sections.body: 16:9 standard · 9:16 shorts · 4:3 legacy. Fixed per variant — never free-form, unlike Image waterfall tiles.

sections.title: Duration format
sections.body: mm:ss under an hour · h:mm:ss over · LIVE for live streams · Shorts label instead of a duration for 9:16.

sections.title: Duration placement
sections.body: bottom-right on 16:9 · bottom-left on 9:16. Deliberate deviation from the Image half’s top-left badge rule.

sections.title: Autoplay
sections.body: Muted by default. Hover-preview on desktop only; tap-to-play on touch. Never autoplay with sound.

sections.title: Safe areas
sections.body: Overlay text sits in the bottom 40% scrim. Keep the top-left clear for content-type badges.

sections.title: Adult gating
sections.body: Blur + interstitial per the Adult video guideline. Applies before any thumbnail renders.

sections.title: Item counts
sections.body: 3–6 items for an inline answer. More warrants a dedicated section or the VRP.

sections.title: Usage
sections.body: Referenced by every Video molecule and cell. When a rule here conflicts with generic ACF guidance, this page wins for MM surfaces.

sections.title: Source discrepancies
sections.body: The written rules above and current component instances are separate source evidence. Short Card documentation supplies 3:4 and 2:3 ratios (Components also includes 9:16); the captured default places its badge at top-left. Vertical Video Group text says Below, while its actual supplied cards use Inline metadata. The website keeps observed component states and records these differences.
